name.la: Pro insipiente et Responsio ad Gaunilonem
name.en-US: Gaunilo’s In Behalf of the Fool and Anselm’s Reply
name.pt-BR: Gaunilo, Em favor do insipiente, e a Resposta de Anselmo

description.la: Gaunilonis monachi Maioris Monasterii Liber pro insipiente adversus Proslogion, et Anselmi Liber apologeticus contra Gaunilonem: disputatio de argumento «id quo maius cogitari nequit». Textus ex editione Migne (Patrologia Latina 158, 1853).
description.en-US: The exchange on the argument of the Proslogion: the monk Gaunilo’s “In Behalf of the Fool” in eight sections (the lost-island objection) and Anselm’s reply in ten chapters. The Latin is the Migne text (Patrologia Latina 158, 1853): Anselm’s reply from a machine-corrected OCR, Gaunilo from Latin Wikisource; the English is Sidney Norton Deane’s 1903 translation, which follows the Latin section for section.
description.pt-BR: A troca de argumentos sobre o Proslógio: o «Em favor do insipiente» do monge Gaunilo, em oito partes (a objeção da ilha perdida), e a resposta de Anselmo, em dez capítulos.

sources.edition: S. Anselmi Cantuariensis archiepiscopi opera omnia, ed. J.-P. Migne, Patrologia Latina 158 (Paris 1853), the Gerberon text; TEI XML of the Corpus Corporum (University of Zurich), text 10624, from the Open Greek and Latin machine-corrected OCR.
sources.description: The complete text with its chapter divisions and PL chapter summaries. PL page breaks, the column numbers and the apparatus of alternative chapter numbers (al.) are dropped; Scripture references stay in parentheses as printed. The OCR carries a few residual slips.
sources.tierEvidence: Anselm died in 1109; Migne’s 1853 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: Gaunilo, Liber pro insipiente adversus S. Anselmi in Proslogio ratiocinationem, as printed in Migne, Patrologia Latina 158 (cols 241-248), from Latin Wikisource.
sources.description: Gaunilo’s eight sections, with the PL column markers dropped.
sources.tierEvidence: Gaunilo wrote in the eleventh century; Migne’s 1853 printing is public domain.

sources.edition: St. Anselm: Proslogium; Monologium; an Appendix in Behalf of the Fool by Gaunilon; and Cur Deus Homo, translated from the Latin by Sidney Norton Deane (Chicago: Open Court, 1903). Christian Classics Ethereal Library plain-text edition.
sources.description: Gaunilon’s “In Behalf of the Fool” and Anselm’s Apologetic (Deane’s introduction and notes are not imported). Chapter titles are Deane’s chapter summaries; translator’s notes are kept as footnotes.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in Chicago in 1903, before 1931: public domain in the US.

title.la: Caput I. Generatim refellitur adversarii ratiocinatio; et ostenditur id quo majus cogitari non potest, esse reipsa
title.en-US: Chapter I. A general refutation of Gaunilon's argument. It is shown that a being than which a greater cannot be conceived exists in reality
title.pt-BR: Capítulo I. Refuta-se em geral o raciocínio do adversário e mostra-se que aquilo do qual não se pode pensar nada maior existe na realidade

title.la: Caput II. Magis urgetur ratiocinatio praeposita; et ostenditur id quo majus cogitari nequit, cogitari posse, atque adeo etiam esse
title.en-US: Chapter II. The argument is continued. It is shown that a being than which a greater is inconceivable can be conceived, and also, in so far, exists
title.pt-BR: Capítulo II. Insiste-se no raciocínio apresentado e mostra-se que aquilo do qual não se pode pensar nada maior pode ser pensado e, por isso, também existe

title.la: Caput III. Ad instantiam adversarii: quod sequeretur insulam fictitiam esse reipsa, quia cogitatur
title.en-US: Chapter III. A criticism of Gaunilon's example, in which he tries to show that in this way the real existence of a lost island might be inferred from the fact of its being conceived
title.pt-BR: Capítulo III. Resposta à objeção do adversário: seguir-se-ia que uma ilha fictícia existe na realidade por ser pensada

title.la: Caput IV. Differentia inter posse cogitari, et intelligi non esse
title.en-US: Chapter IV. The difference between the possibility of conceiving of non-existence, and understanding non-existence
title.pt-BR: Capítulo IV. Diferença entre poder pensar e entender que algo não existe

title.la: Caput V. Specialis discussio variorum adversarii dictorum: ac primum quod initio infideliter retulerit ratiocinationem, quam refellendam suscepit
title.en-US: Chapter V. A particular discussion of certain statements of Gaunilon's. In the first place, he misquoted the argument which he undertook to refute
title.pt-BR: Capítulo V. Exame particular de diversas afirmações do adversário: primeiro, que no início expôs sem fidelidade o raciocínio que se propôs refutar

title.la: Caput VI. Discutitur dictum adversarii in num. 2, quaelibet falsa similiter possent intelligi, atque adeo essent
title.en-US: Chapter VI. A discussion of Gaunilon's argument in his second chapter: that any unreal beings can be understood in the same way, and would, to that extent, exist
title.pt-BR: Capítulo VI. Examina-se a afirmação do adversário no n. 2: quaisquer coisas falsas poderiam ser igualmente entendidas e, por isso, existiriam

title.la: Caput VII. Contra dictum aliud adversarii ibidem: nempe quod summum magnum aeque possit concipi non esse; ac Deus ab insipiente concipitur
title.en-US: Chapter VII. In answer to another objection: that the supremely great being may be conceived not to exist, just as by the fool God is conceived not to exist
title.pt-BR: Capítulo VII. Contra outra afirmação do adversário no mesmo lugar: pode-se pensar que o sumamente grande não existe, assim como o insipiente pensa que Deus não existe

title.la: Caput VIII. Comparatio picturae num. 3 proposita examinatur. Et unde conjici queat summum magnum, de quo adversarius num. 4 quaesierat
title.en-US: Chapter VIII. The example of the picture, treated in Gaunilon's third chapter, is examined.--From what source a notion may be formed of the supremely great being, of which Gaunilon inquired in his fourth chapter
title.pt-BR: Capítulo VIII. Examina-se a comparação da pintura proposta no n. 3 e de onde se pode formar uma noção do sumamente grande, questão levantada pelo adversário no n. 4

title.la: Caput IX. Summum magnum cogitari et intelligi posse: et roboratur ratio contra insipientem facta
title.en-US: Chapter IX. The possibility of understanding and conceiving of the supremely great being. The argument advanced against the fool is confirmed
title.pt-BR: Capítulo IX. O sumamente grande pode ser pensado e entendido; confirma-se o argumento apresentado contra o insipiente

title.la: Caput X. Firmitas rationis praedictae, et libelli clausula
title.en-US: Chapter X. The certainty of the foregoing argument.--The conclusion of the book
title.pt-BR: Capítulo X. Firmeza do argumento precedente e conclusão do opúsculo
